1.word_for_word: sapta-viṃśe — in the twenty-seventh chapter; tad ālakṣya — recognizing that; kṛṣṇasya prābhavam param — Kṛṣṇa's supreme power; surabhi-indrābhyām — by Surabhi and Indra; abhiṣeka-mahotsavaḥ varṇyate — the great festival of his consecration is described; govardhane dhṛte śaile — after Govardhana had been held up; śakrasya bhayena āgamane hetuḥ — this is the cause of Śakra's coming in fear; āsārāt rakṣite vraje — when Vraja had been saved from the downpour; surabheḥ harṣeṇa āgamane — this is the cause of Surabhi's coming in joy
1.translation: In the twenty-seventh chapter, after Kṛṣṇa's supreme power had become evident, the great consecration performed by Surabhi and Indra is described. Indra comes in fear after seeing Govardhana held aloft, whereas Surabhi comes in joy because Vraja and the cows have been saved from the deluge.

2.word_for_word: tatra indraḥ āgatya kim kṛtavān — what Indra did after arriving; vivikte upasaṅgamya — approaching in a solitary place; prāktana-granthena — described in the text before the words about Surabhi; vivikte — in seclusion; pādayoḥ pasparśa — he touched Kṛṣṇa's feet; namaḥ cakāra — he bowed down
2.translation: What did Indra do when he arrived? The text before Surabhi's appearance explains it: approaching Kṛṣṇa privately in a secluded place, Indra touched his feet and bowed down.

3.word_for_word: śrutaḥ ca asau anubhāvaḥ — Kṛṣṇa's greatness had been heard of and now experienced; dṛṣṭaḥ śruta-anubhāvaḥ yena — Indra had now seen the power he had heard about; naṣṭaḥ tri-lokeśaḥ aham iti madaḥ yasya — his pride ‘I am lord of the three worlds’ was destroyed
3.translation: Indra had now directly seen the power of Kṛṣṇa whose greatness he had previously only heard about. His intoxication with the thought ‘I am lord of the three worlds’ was destroyed.

4.word_for_word: mama aparādham kṣamasva iti vaktum — before asking forgiveness for his offense; tava tāvat aparādhaḥ na asti eva — he first acknowledges that from Kṛṣṇa's side there is no wrongdoing; tvayā anugrahaḥ eva kṛtaḥ — what Kṛṣṇa did was grace alone; viśuddha-sattvam iti — beginning with ‘pure sattva’; dhāma — essential nature; śāntam eka-rūpam — peaceful and unchanging; tapo-mayam — consisting abundantly of knowledge; sarvajñam — omniscient; dhvasta-rajas-tamaskam — in whom rajas and tamas are absent; māyā-kārya-rūpaḥ guṇa-saṃpravāhaḥ — the flow of guṇas that constitutes saṃsāra, an effect of māyā; sa te na vidyate — it does not exist in you; agrahaṇena ajñānena anubadhyate — such bondage follows from non-apprehension, ignorance; sarvajñasya te na asti — this cannot belong to the omniscient Lord
4.translation: Before asking forgiveness, Indra acknowledges that Kṛṣṇa has not truly wronged him at all; Kṛṣṇa's chastisement was grace. ‘Your abode is pure sattva’ means that Kṛṣṇa's essential nature is peaceful, uniform and full of knowledge—omniscient, with rajas and tamas wholly absent. The stream of material qualities that forms saṃsāra in beings like Indra is an effect of māyā and does not exist in Kṛṣṇa. Such bondage follows from ignorance or non-apprehension, and therefore cannot belong to the omniscient Lord.

5.word_for_word: ajñāna-tat-kṛta-deha-sambandhau na staḥ — ignorance and the bodily relation produced by it do not exist in Kṛṣṇa; tat-kṛtānām lobha-ādīnām kā vārtā — how much less greed and other passions produced by that relation; tat-kṛtāḥ deha-sambandha-kṛtāḥ — produced by bodily identification; tad-dhetavaḥ punar anyasya dehasya hetavaḥ — and in turn causes of further embodiment; jñāninām api te dṛśyante iti cet — objection: such traits seem even in knowers; abudha-liṅga-bhāvāḥ — they are marks of ignorance; yāvat rāga-ādi-mattvam tāvat jñānitvam na siddham — as long as attachment and the like remain, true knowledge is not established; tathāpi — nevertheless; man-māna-bhaṅgaḥ daṇḍa-artham — the breaking of my pride was disciplinary punishment
5.translation: If Kṛṣṇa has neither ignorance nor the bodily identification born of ignorance, then greed and the other passions produced by bodily identification cannot belong to him either. Those passions are themselves causes of further embodiment. If one objects that such traits sometimes seem to appear in people called knowers, Śrīdhara answers that attachment and the like are precisely marks of ignorance; where they truly remain, perfect knowledge has not yet been established. Even though Kṛṣṇa is untouched by such passions, however, he broke Indra's pride for the sake of correction.

6.word_for_word: tvat-daṇḍe mama gopa-putrasya kā śaktiḥ — objection: what power could a cowherd's son have to punish me; kim vā kāraṇam — what would be the reason; kaḥ vā daṇḍaḥ mayā kṛtaḥ — what punishment did I actually undergo; tvam pitā jagatām — you are father of the worlds; guruḥ upadeṣṭā — teacher and instructor; adhīśaḥ niyantā — supreme ruler and controller; iti daṇḍa-dhāraṇe hetu-trayam — these are three grounds for bearing the rod of discipline; kālatvāt samarthaḥ — as Time, you have the power; upātta-daṇḍaḥ hitāya — you assume punishment for welfare; sva-icchā-tanubhiḥ līlā-avatāraiḥ — through forms assumed by your own will, your playful descents; jagad-īśa-māninām māna-vidhūnanam — your play removes the pride of those who imagine themselves lords of the world
6.translation: One might ask, ‘What authority has a cowherd boy to punish Indra? For what reason, and what was the punishment?’ Indra answers that Kṛṣṇa is the father of the worlds, their teacher, and their supreme ruler—three grounds for wielding corrective discipline. As Time he has the power to do so, and for the welfare of beings he assumes the rod through forms manifested by his own will. The very play of his descents consists, among other things, in shaking away the pride of those like Indra who imagine themselves rulers of the world.

7.word_for_word: mad-vidhāḥ ajñāḥ — ignorant persons like me; jagad-īśa-māninaḥ — who imagine themselves lords of the world; bhaya-kāle api — even at a time of danger; tvām abhayam bhayam agaṇayantam vīkṣya — seeing you fearless and disregarding danger; āśu tat-madam hitvā — quickly abandoning that pride; vigata-garvāḥ — freed of arrogance; ārya-mārgam tvad-bhakti-lakṣaṇam bhajanti — follow the noble path characterized by devotion to you; tava īhā eva svakānām anuśāsanam — your actions themselves are the discipline of your own servants
7.translation: Ignorant people like Indra may imagine themselves universal rulers, but when a crisis comes and they see Kṛṣṇa utterly fearless, treating danger as nothing, they quickly abandon such pride. Freed from arrogance, they return to the noble path marked by devotion to him. Thus Kṛṣṇa's own actions are themselves the discipline by which he corrects those who belong to him.

8.word_for_word: bhagavat-svarūpam abhiprāyam ca anuvārṇya — having described the Lord's nature and intention; kṣamāpayati — Indra asks forgiveness; sa tvam iti — beginning ‘you are that Lord’; evaṃ-bhūtā asatī matiḥ me punaḥ mā bhūt — may such a false state of mind never arise in me again
8.translation: Having described Kṛṣṇa's nature and the purpose of his chastisement, Indra asks forgiveness. He adds another prayer: ‘May such a false and distorted mentality never arise in me again.’

9.word_for_word: mahān ayam aparādhaḥ katham kṣantavyaḥ — how can so great an offense be forgiven; tava iti — he answers with the verse beginning ‘your’; bhārāṇām — burdens upon the earth; uru-bhāra-janmanām — those from whom many great burdens arise; abhavāya nāśāya — for their destruction; yuṣmat-caraṇa-sevinām tu bhavāya — but for the welfare of those who serve your feet; mama tvat-sevakatvāt — because I too am your servant; atyanta-aparādhinaḥ api kṣantavyam — even my severe offense should therefore be forgiven
9.translation: How can an offense this great be forgiven? Indra appeals to the purpose of Kṛṣṇa's descent: he destroys those from whom great burdens upon the earth arise, but brings welfare to servants of his feet. ‘Since I too am your servant,’ Indra implies, ‘forgive me despite the gravity of my offense.’

10.word_for_word: kṣamāpayan namaskaroti — while asking forgiveness he bows; tubhyam bhagavate kṛṣṇāya namaḥ — obeisance to you, Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa; puruṣāya sarva-antaryāmiṇe — to the Puruṣa, inner controller of all; mahātmane — the great Self; antaḥ-sthatve api aparicchinnāya — though dwelling within, not limited; vāsudevāya — to Vāsudeva; sarva-nivāsāya — abode of all; sātvatām yādavānām pataye — Lord of the Sātvatas, the Yādavas
10.translation: Indra bows as he seeks forgiveness: ‘Obeisance to you, Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, the Puruṣa and inner controller of all, the great Self who, though dwelling within all things, is not limited by them; to Vāsudeva, the abode of all, Lord of the Sātvatas and Yādavas.’

11.word_for_word: tarhi kim aham yādavaḥ — does this mean the Lord is merely a Yādava; na — no; svacchanda-upātta-dehāya — whose body is assumed freely; sveṣām bhaktānām chandena icchayā svīkṛta-dehāya — who accepts a form by his own wish and for the desire of his devotees; viśuddham jñānam eva mūrtiḥ yasya — whose form is pure consciousness itself; māyayā sarvasmai sarva-rūpāya — through māyā appearing as all forms; sarvasya bījāya kāraṇāya — seed and cause of everything; sarva-bhūta-ātmane — Self of all beings
11.translation: Calling him Lord of the Yādavas does not restrict Kṛṣṇa to being an ordinary member of that clan. He freely assumes a body by his own will and in response to the desire of his devotees, and that form is pure consciousness itself. Through his māyā he appears as all forms, because he is the seed and cause of all and therefore the Self of every being.

12.word_for_word: kṛta-āgasaḥ iti anena uktam aparādham nivedayati — Indra now states the offense implied by ‘having committed sin’; mayā idam — this was done by me; āsāra-vāyubhiḥ — with torrents and winds; goṣṭha-nāśāya — for the destruction of Vraja; akṛtyam ceṣṭitam kṛtam — I carried out a deed that should never have been done
12.translation: Indra now explicitly confesses the offense: ‘With torrents of rain and violent winds I attempted to destroy the cowherd settlement. I did what should never have been done.’

13.word_for_word: tathā api bho īśa — nevertheless, O Lord; tvayā anugṛhītaḥ asmi — I have been favored by you; dhvasta-stambhaḥ — my arrogance has been destroyed; vṛthā-udyamaḥ — my hostile effort was made futile
13.translation: ‘Nevertheless, O Lord, you have favored me.’ Indra identifies the grace: Kṛṣṇa shattered his arrogance and rendered his destructive effort completely futile.

14.word_for_word: indreṇa sva-abhiprāye nivedite — after Indra disclosed his state of mind; bhagavān api tathā eva āha — Bhagavān confirms it; mayā iti — with the verse beginning ‘by me’; indra-śriyā — through the prosperity and splendor of Indra; deva-rājyena — the kingship of the gods
14.translation: After Indra has explained his understanding, Bhagavān confirms it in the verse beginning ‘by me.’ ‘Indra's fortune’ means the royal splendor and sovereignty of being king of the gods.

15-16.word_for_word: indreṇa sva-abhiprāye nivedite — after Indra expressed his realization; bhagavān api tathā eva āha — Bhagavān affirmed the same point; indra-śriyā — by Indra's royal prosperity; deva-rājyena — the sovereignty of the gods
15-16.translation: These verses continue Kṛṣṇa's response to Indra's confession: the very splendor and sovereignty that belong to Indra had become the occasion of pride, and Kṛṣṇa's action was intended to correct that pride.

17.word_for_word: vaḥ — by you, plural; bahu-vacanam varuṇa-ādi-abhiprāyeṇa — the plural also includes Varuṇa and other gods; kva gantavyam — where should I go; svarge api tava eva īśvaratvāt — since even in heaven you are the true Lord; kriyatām iti — Kṛṣṇa replies ‘let it be done’; mad-anuśāsanena yathā-pūrvam tatra sthīyatām — remain in your office as before, under my command; yuktaiḥ apramattaiḥ — attentive and vigilant; stambha-varjitaiḥ nirahaṅkāraiḥ — free from stiffness, pride and ego
17.translation: The plural form is intentionally broader than Indra and includes Varuṇa and other divine rulers. If Indra thinks, ‘Where can I go, since even in heaven you alone are Lord?’ Kṛṣṇa replies: ‘Return and perform your office as before, but do so under my command—attentive, vigilant and free from arrogance.’

18.word_for_word: sva-santānaiḥ gobhiḥ saha — together with her offspring, the cows; upāmantrya — approaching and addressing him; kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa iti-ādi-sambodhya — calling ‘Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa!’ and so on
18.translation: Surabhi then approached with her cow progeny and addressed the Lord with invocations beginning ‘Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa!’

19.word_for_word: indreṇa hatāḥ api — though attacked by Indra; bhavatā sa-nāthāḥ vayam kṛtāḥ — by you we have been given a protector; rakṣitāḥ — we have been saved
19.translation: Surabhi says: ‘Though Indra attacked us, you made us people who possess a true protector—you saved us.’

20.word_for_word: tvam naḥ paramam daivam devatā — you are our supreme deity; jagat-pate — O Lord of the world; go-vipra-devānām — of cows, brāhmaṇas and gods; ye anye ca sādhavaḥ — and all other virtuous beings; teṣām bhavāya abhyudayāya — for their welfare and flourishing; adya tvam eva naḥ indraḥ bhava — today you alone be our Indra
20.translation: ‘You are our supreme deity. O Lord of the world, for the welfare and flourishing of the cows, brāhmaṇas, gods and all other righteous beings, become today our true Indra—our sovereign protector.’

21.word_for_word: bhavatām indraḥ asti iti cet — objection: but you already have Indra; alam purandarasya indratayā — enough of Purandara's status as our Indra; devaḥ eva indraḥ bhavati katham aham — objection: only a god becomes Indra, how can Kṛṣṇa; avatīrṇaḥ asi iti — the answer is ‘you have descended’
21.translation: If one says, ‘But the cows already have Indra,’ Surabhi's answer is that Purandara has proved insufficient as their sovereign. If another objects that an Indra should be a heavenly god, the response is that Kṛṣṇa himself has descended into the world and is therefore fully able to assume that role.

22.word_for_word: surabhiḥ ātmanaḥ payasā abhyaṣiñcat — Surabhi consecrated him with her own milk; indraḥ ākāśa-gaṅgāyā jalaiḥ abhyaṣiñcat — Indra consecrated him with waters of the celestial Gaṅgā; deva-mātṛbhiḥ aditi-ādibhiḥ — together with divine mothers such as Aditi, or with gods and mothers; gāḥ paśūn — cows/animals; gām svargam vā — or the earth/heaven; indratvena vindati — he obtains/protects them in the capacity of Indra; govinda iti abhyadhāt — he named him Govinda
22.translation: Surabhi bathed Kṛṣṇa with her own milk, and Indra bathed him with the waters of the celestial Gaṅgā. The accompanying phrase may refer to divine mothers such as Aditi, or separately to gods and mothers. Indra then bestowed the name ‘Govinda’: one who, as the true sovereign, protects and possesses the cows—while ‘go’ can also extend to the earth or heavenly realm.

25.word_for_word: deva-nikāyeṣu ketavaḥ iva — like banners among the hosts of gods; darśanīyāḥ mukhyāḥ — conspicuous and foremost; gāvaḥ gām pṛthvīm — the cows made the earth; payobhiḥ drutām ārdrām — flowing and moist with their milk; anayan akurvan — they made it so
25.translation: The foremost gods shone conspicuously among the celestial hosts like banners. The cows, meanwhile, drenched the earth with streams of their milk.

26.word_for_word: nānā-rasa-oghāḥ — streams of many kinds of liquid; kṣīra-ādi-vāhinyaḥ — carrying milk and other substances; akṛṣṭa-pacyāḥ — ripening without cultivation; oṣadhayaḥ vrīhi-ādayaḥ — crops such as rice; girayaḥ — mountains; unmaṇīn — jewels emerging outward; garbha-gatān maṇīn ut udagatān bahiḥ prakaṭān — gems formerly within the mountains appearing openly outside
26.translation: Streams flowed with many kinds of nourishing liquids such as milk; crops such as rice ripened without cultivation. Alternatively, the phrase may qualify the mountains: where such uncultivated plants grew, the mountains also brought forth their jewels, gems formerly hidden within them becoming openly visible.
